reports.title: H&R Block Reports Fiscal 2027 First Quarter Results and Reaffirms Fiscal 2027 Outlook

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook Reaffirmed
section: •Revenue to be in the range of $4.11 to $4.16 billion.
•Adjusted EBITDA4 to be in the range of $1.11 to $1.14 billion.
•Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share4 to be in the range of $6.04 to $6.24.

desk.headline: Off-season revenue up 10% to $224.3m, beat; seasonal loss smaller than expected; fiscal 2027 outlook reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose 10.2% to $224.3m in the quiet pre-tax-season quarter, beating the $212.3m estimate, helped by international, tax protection and small business services.
Operating costs rose 11.1% to $456.2m, including $8.0m of severance from changing office leadership, so the usual seasonal loss widened.
Adjusted loss per share was $1.40 versus $1.20 a year ago, but smaller than the $1.45 loss analysts expected; the GAAP loss was $1.53.
The company bought back $100.3m of shares and declared a $0.46 quarterly dividend; about $500m of the buyback plan remains.

guidance.summary: H&R Block kept its full fiscal 2027 outlook unchanged. The Q1 severance charge is excluded from the adjusted targets.

points: A new advisory-style office model, where tax pros prepare before meeting clients, is being tested in about 650 offices this season, up from five.
An AI-assisted review of new clients' past returns is being expanded; management said its effect on retention is not yet proven.
Most of the international growth came from currency moves; small business growth was led by the Wave subscription product.
About $400m of buybacks is planned for fiscal 2027, and an Investor Day on 3 December will set out a three-year plan.
Spending on strategic projects rises in Q2 (about $12m vs $6m in Q1), but revenue is still expected to grow faster than costs for the year.
